nodes.content: Design live firmware updates for an embedded controller that preserve real-time deadlines and actuator consistency across state-schema changes.
requirements: Maintain 1 ms control deadlines throughout uninterrupted updates, without duplicated or skipped actuator commands.
Reject incompatible state migrations atomically; recover a compatible firmware-state pair after any update-time reset.

nodes.content: Run an immutable 1-ms control island with sequence-gated actuator writes; atomically commit validated firmware-state pairs via dual-slot descriptors.
How can dual-slot commits recover a compatible firmware-state pair if power fails between migration validation and descriptor activation?
Checksummed, schema-validated firmware-state slots with final-write monotonic commit markers let boot recover a compatible pair after every write-boundary reset.
Specify validation and marker-write ordering; inject resets at every flash-write boundary; verify boot selects a compatible committed pair.
Run SlotCrash-1, resetting after each firmware, migrated-state, CRC, and commit-marker write; assert boot loads matching committed generations.
SlotCrash-1 reset matrix records each write-boundary injection, slot CRC, commit generation, and boot-selected firmware-state schema pair.
Audit SlotCrash-1 reset matrix for complete write-boundary coverage and CRC-valid, schema-compatible boot pairs after each reset.
SlotCrash-1 covered 47/47 write boundaries; every reset booted a CRC-valid, schema-matched committed pair, never a partially migrated slot.
Adopt final-write monotonic commit markers for slot activation; SlotCrash-1 recovered compatible pairs at all 47 tested write boundaries.
Run SchemaFault-1 with incompatible migrations and resets at every flash-write boundary; verify unchanged descriptors and compatible boot pairs.
SchemaFault-1 rejected 12/12 incompatible migrations; all 36 reachable write-boundary resets retained the previous compatible firmware-state pair.
A SchemaFault-1 write-boundary reset after an incompatible migration activates a descriptor pointing to mismatched firmware and state.
Trace commit-marker writes during rejected SchemaFault-1 migrations; reboot at 36 reset points and check firmware-state schema compatibility.
With fallback-slot CRC corrupted, 1/36 SchemaFault-1 resets activated a v3-firmware/v2-state descriptor after migration rejection.
After 1/36 corrupted-fallback resets mismatched schemas, require validated fallback before activation and boot an immutable compatible recovery pair otherwise.
Stage firmware asynchronously; switch at 1-ms tick boundaries using prevalidated state buffers and single-writer, sequence-gated actuator commits.
Can tick-boundary handoff preserve every 1-ms deadline and exactly one actuator write per sequence during state-schema conversion?
Prevalidated shadow-state conversion and a ≤40-µs tick-boundary swap preserve 1-ms deadlines with exactly one actuator commit per sequence.
Run TickSwap-1 for 10⁶ ticks with v2→v3 conversions; log deadline misses, swap latency, and actuator sequence gaps or duplicates.
TickSwap-1 logged two duplicate actuator writes across 10⁶ ticks, despite zero deadline misses and 31-µs maximum swap latency.
Use a fixed 1-ms actuator dispatcher with fenced firmware producers, per-tick command selection, and fallback commands during handoff.
How should the dispatcher fence stale producers and choose a safe command when the new firmware misses its first tick?
Specify atomic producer-epoch fencing and a prevalidated safe-hold command; test delayed first ticks for deadline, gap, and duplicate violations.
Implement epoch-tagged command slots and a dispatcher-only write gate; inject 0–3-tick new-producer delays in FenceTick-1.
FenceTick-1 dispatcher patch adds epoch-tagged command slots, a sole actuator-write gate, and prevalidated safe-hold output for delayed producers.
Run FenceTick-1 on the patched dispatcher across 0–3-tick producer delays; measure deadline misses and per-sequence actuator gaps or duplicates.
FenceTick-1 logged zero deadline misses, actuator sequence gaps, or duplicate writes across 4 million ticks; safe-hold covered delayed producers.
Stress FenceTick-1 with stale-epoch writes racing handoff and 3-tick producer stalls; verify rejection, safe-hold selection, and 1-ms deadlines.
FenceTick-1 emitted two stale-epoch commands instead of safe-hold during handoff races, violating actuator consistency despite zero deadline misses.
Reject the dispatcher patch despite its 4-million-tick pass; require atomic epoch validation at actuator commit after two stale-command race failures.
Combine immutable 1-ms dispatcher, atomic commit-time epoch fencing, safe-hold commands, and dual-slot schema-validated firmware-state pairs with immutable recovery.
How can firmware-state pair activation synchronize with commit-time epoch fencing without delaying a 1-ms dispatch or exposing mismatched state?
After background validation, a ≤25-µs tick-boundary atomic pair-pointer/epoch swap preserves 1-ms deadlines and prevents mismatched or stale actuator commands.
Run PairFence-1 with atomic pair/epoch swaps, stale-producer races, and resets; measure swap latency, deadline misses, and stale/schema-mismatched commits.
PairFence-1 recorded a 44-µs swap and one 1-ms deadline miss under flash contention across 10⁶ ticks.
Schedule flash writes in certified idle windows; rerun PairFence-1 measuring swap latency, deadline misses, stale commands, and boot-pair compatibility.
Idle-window PairFence-1 achieved 19-µs maximum swaps, zero deadline misses or stale/schema-mismatched actuator commits across 10⁶ ticks.
Adopt idle-window flash scheduling: it reduced maximum swap latency from 44 to 19 µs and eliminated the observed deadline miss.
Run bounded, schema-typed migrations in shadow slots; reject actuator-invariant failures before activation and retain the previous committed pair.
Which v2→v3 actuator-state invariants must shadow migration check to prevent an unsafe command jump at activation?
Preserved actuator mode, next-command sequence, ≤0.2 N·m torque discontinuity, and ≤1 N·m/ms slew reject unsafe v2→v3 migrations.
Define v2→v3 migration contracts, generate boundary and corrupt-state fixtures, then test atomic rejection and first-command actuator continuity.
Implement MigrationContract-v3 checking mode, next sequence, 0.2-N·m torque jump, and 1-N·m/ms slew before shadow-slot commit.
MigrationContract-v3 specifies v2→v3 field mappings, actuator invariants, rejection codes, and a shadow-slot validator that leaves active descriptors unchanged.
Run MigrationBoundary-1 against MigrationContract-v3 with mode/sequence faults, torque jumps, slew-limit boundaries, and reset injections; verify atomic rejection and first-command continuity.
MigrationBoundary-1 atomically rejected 48/48 invariant violations; 24 valid cases met torque/slew limits; 36 resets preserved compatible pairs.
Adopt MigrationContract-v3 for v2→v3 activation: all 48 invalid migrations rejected atomically, and valid first commands met actuator limits.
